basis: Manifesting carriers have skeletal muscle myopathy; respiratory involvement is variable and not established above 30% for this subgroup.
Skeletal dysplasia affecting vertebrae and long-bone metaphyses; no qualifying extraskeletal damage.
Schizophrenia is a psychiatric disorder without a qualifying organ axis.
Microbial infection and inflammation of the peritoneum; secondary multiorgan dysfunction is not a defining organ manifestation.
Developmental defects of parietal bones and clavicles; the definition explicitly reports no dental abnormalities.
Inherited cataract with impaired vision; reported manifestations remain within the ocular axis.
Isolated congenital absence or dystrophy of nails.
Glycosylation defect with platelet/neutrophil abnormalities; pulmonary hemorrhage 80-99% in supplied HPO; neurodevelopmental impairment common in reported cases; tiny cohorts.
Growth-factor deficiency with lipodystrophy and skin thickening; contractures/joint stiffness 80-99%. Atherosclerosis is a separately diagnosed vascular disease.
Malignant tumor originating in bone; systemic inflammatory blood findings do not establish a separate damaged organ.
Structural prolapse of urethral mucosa; the urethra belongs to the renal axis.
Fanconi anemia; anal atresia 2/2, renal abnormalities at least 1/3 including severe renal failure, and radial/thumb defects 1/3; estimates derive from very small cohorts.
Spastic neurodegeneration and sensorineural deafness define disease; cataract/visual impairment and hypogonadism each occur in 30-79%.
KCNT1-related developmental epileptic encephalopathy; hypotonia is neurologic, and seizure-associated cardiac changes do not establish cardiovascular damage.
Inherited susceptibility alone establishes neither active lymphoma nor blood or immune dysfunction; no current organ disease is specified.
Marrow failure is a principal phenotype of ACD-related telomere disease; pulmonary, hepatic and skin damage are not established as common across this broad umbrella.
Neoplastic occupation of the peritoneum; no additional organ involvement is established across this heterogeneous group.
A disorder defined by urethral dysfunction; infection is not required.
Mitochondrial respiratory-chain defect with lactic acidosis 3/3; neurologic disease includes infantile spasms/hypsarrhythmia in 1/3. Optic damage frequency is unspecified.
Inherited digestive enzyme deficiency causes lipid malabsorption and steatorrhea; pancreatic exocrine function is affected despite no structural pancreatic disease.
Congenital sensory neuropathy impairs pain perception; injuries and their complications are secondary consequences rather than direct involvement of other organs.
Corticotropin-producing neoplasm originates in the pituitary endocrine gland; separately diagnosed consequences of hypercortisolism are excluded.
Hypogonadotropic hypogonadism defines disease; congenital anosmia and osteopenia each occur in 2/3 reported patients, supporting sensory and skeletal involvement.
Paralytic failure of eyelid closure defines this eyelid disorder; an underlying facial neuropathy is a separate causal condition.
Defined by disease of auditory neural pathways, including the vestibulocochlear nerve, brainstem or central auditory nervous system.
